questions.question: What problem does this paper address and what is its main approach?
questions.gold_answer: Dominant sequence transduction models rely on recurrent or convolutional networks, whose sequential computation limits parallelization and makes training slow. The paper proposes the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based solely on (multi-head self-)attention with no recurrence or convolution, which achieves state-of-the-art BLEU on WMT 2014 English-German and English-French translation at a fraction of the training cost and also generalizes to English constituency parsing.
evidence: based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
This inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples

questions.question: What is the purpose of this paper and how is it organised?
questions.gold_answer: The paper introduces retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe that combines a pre-trained seq2seq generator (BART) as parametric memory with a dense Wikipedia index accessed by a pre-trained DPR retriever as non-parametric memory, comparing RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token formulations. It is organised into an introduction, methods (models, retriever, generator, training, decoding), experiments and results on open-domain QA, abstractive QA, Jeopardy question generation and FEVER fact verification plus ablations and index hot-swapping, then related work, discussion, broader impact and appendices with implementation details.
evidence: We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia
and fine-tune end-to-end

questions.question: What is the purpose of this document and how is it organised?
questions.gold_answer: The NIST AI RMF 1.0 is a voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific framework to help organizations manage the risks of AI systems and promote trustworthy and responsible AI. Part 1 frames AI risk, describes the audience, and outlines the characteristics of trustworthy AI; Part 2 presents the Core's four functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) with categories and subcategories, plus AI RMF profiles, followed by appendices on AI actor tasks, how AI risks differ from traditional software, human-AI interaction, and framework attributes.
evidence: The Framework is divided into two parts. Part 1 discusses how organizations can frame
It describes four specific functions to help organizations address the risks of AI systems in practice
